purpose: Declared record of the v3 screening rows. A screening row is NOT a continuation of a v2.2 learning-rate family: it changes the architecture and is initialized from -- not resumed from -- a parent checkpoint. Keeping these rows out of exhibition/data/continuation_history.csv is deliberate. Mixing them into calibrated_lr3e4 would place a different architecture on that family's continuous loss axis and would let a v3 row compete for a v2.2 family's accepted best.
promotion_rule: Retain the simpler parent when an improvement is statistically unresolved. A screening row is promoted only when its declared target improves AND every declared guard passes.
selection_role: Screening rows are development evidence. They do not select or tune any published checkpoint and they never touch the test split.

loss_measure_contract.common_response_nll_measure: negative log density in deposited-energy GeV
loss_measure_contract.validation_reduction: mean of per-batch scalars, exactly matching the trainer including the final partial batch
loss_measure_contract.within_run_checkpoint_selection_effect: none; the offset is fixed for this validation loader

rows.label: M0 · zero-axis control, fresh optimizer
rows.scientific_question: How much of S1's shortfall is the fresh optimizer rather than the axis features?
rows.loss_weight_schema: v2.2 keys only; this row adds no loss term

initialization.note: Deliberately fresh, matching S1 exactly. That is the point of the control.

control.match: identical architecture, parameter count, input width, seed, data order, bank, batch, accumulation, schedule, solver steps, update count and stopping rule
control.mismatch: S1 feeds computed incident-axis values where this row feeds zeros

second_control.match: no axis information, same parent, same horizon
second_control.mismatch: dicos-f-03 resumed optimizer state; this row starts fresh

rows.reads: Near dicos-f-03's 4.491971 means the fresh optimizer explains most of S1's shortfall. Near S1's 4.514053 means the optimizer is the dominant term and the axis feature is not the story. Near B0 means both cost something.
rows.mathematical_note: With identically zero axis input the axis weight block receives zero gradient and stays zero for the whole run, so this row is mathematically a v2.2 model trained with a fresh optimizer while keeping S1's exact parameter count.
rows.evidence_gap: no per-epoch distribution diagnostics: launched through dicos_train.py rather than the campaign supervisor, so nothing was staged into _diag/
rows.disposition_reason: M0 is a control, not a promotion candidate: it carries no feature to promote. It completed its full 24-epoch horizon with best validation loss 4.513572058600877 at epoch 19, the same epoch S1 peaked at.

vs_s1_axis.reading: The axis feature is NEUTRAL. S1 and M0 differ by 0.000481, which is below the 0.001259 run-to-run reference, so the two are indistinguishable. Feeding real incident-axis coordinates instead of zeros changed nothing measurable.

vs_dicos_f_03.reading: This is the FRESH-OPTIMIZER COST, isolated. f-03 resumed its optimizer state; M0 started a fresh Adam. Nothing else differs: both carry no axis information, both fork from the same parent, both run 24 epochs.

attribution_of_s1_shortfall.statement: S1's entire shortfall against dicos-f-03 is the fresh optimizer. The axis feature accounts for 0.00048 of 0.02208, which is below the reproducibility reference.

rows.label: S1 · incident-axis features
rows.scientific_question: Do incident-axis-relative node coordinates lower the validation loss?
rows.loss_weight_schema: v2.2 keys only; this row adds no loss term

initialization.note: initialize_from transfers weights only. The row therefore starts with a fresh Adam while its control, dicos-f-03, resumed its optimizer. This is a real confound on any head-to-head loss comparison.

control.match: same parent checkpoint (dicos-f-02 e90), same 24-epoch horizon, same re-heat peak learning rate
control.mismatch: resumed optimizer state; no axis features

rows.disposition_reason: The completed configuration was worse in validation loss than both its parent (4.483768) and its matched no-axis control (4.491971). Under the frozen promotion rule the simpler parent is retained and axis features stay off in downstream configs.
rows.causal_reason: RESOLVED by M0-fresh on 2026-08-15. M0 is identical to S1 in architecture, parameter count, input width, seed, data order, bank, batch, accumulation, schedule, solver steps, update count and stopping rule, and differs only by feeding zero axis values instead of computed ones. M0 reached 4.513572 against S1's 4.514053, a difference of 0.000481 -- below the 0.001259 run-to-run reference. The axis feature is neutral. S1's 0.022082 shortfall against dicos-f-03 is almost entirely the fresh optimizer (0.021601), which M0 isolates.

checkpoints.format_defect: The trainer saved this v3 run through the v2.2 path, so architecture_version is null and the format-4 adversarial-resume fields are absent. The weights and frozen config are correct and the run's result stands, but this checkpoint is not a valid adversarial-resume source. Immutable: it must never be rewritten or re-stamped.

rows.evidence_gap: This row was launched through dicos_train.py directly rather than the campaign supervisor, so no checkpoints were staged into _diag/ and no per-epoch distribution diagnostics exist. Loss, structural invariants and fixed-condition visualizations are complete. The distribution evidence is recoverable only by evaluating the retained best checkpoint through the validation metric battery.

rows.label: S2 · bounded response spline
rows.scientific_question: Does a bounded conditional spline with one zero atom beat the clamped mixture?
rows.inheritance_note: S2 does NOT inherit S1's axis features. S1 was not promoted, and the original matrix's cumulative chain assumed every row promotes. Inheritance is now opt-in and must name promoted rows.
rows.loss_weight_schema: v2.2 keys only; the spline replaces the response head rather than adding a term

comparator.why: M0 is the fresh-optimizer control. Its historical raw loss is converted to the same deposited-energy-GeV response-density measure as S2 before comparison.

initialization.note: expanded 0 because this row adds no axis columns; the 15 initialized tensors are the new bounded spline response head. That head starts untrained, so this row's epoch 0 is legitimately high (5.064650) -- unlike S1 and M0, whose migrations were behavioural no-ops. initialize_from, its sha256 and preflight were all verified correct.

rows.scientific_motivation: the v2.2 clamped mixture creates a second zero atom; the bounded spline removes it. Justified as a structural repair, not an AUROC fix: the zero-only AUROC bound is at most 0.507 against a measured 0.843.
rows.queued_behind: M0-fresh, via _v3/chain_m0_then_s2.sh, which refuses to start unless M0 completes its full declared horizon

rows.label: S3 · hierarchical ECAL/HCAL first layer
rows.scientific_question: Does factorizing the first layer fix the underproduced ECAL-start prevalence?
rows.inheritance_note: S3 forks from B0 in isolation, not from S2. Stacking a promoted feature is a separate declared experiment and a judgment call on the evidence, which a queue script is not allowed to make. This row measures the hierarchical first layer alone.
rows.loss_weight_schema: v2.2 keys plus ecal_start and hcal_first at 0.5 each. Those two terms have never trained before this row, and 0.5 is a deliberate unweighted-first placeholder, not a tuned value.

loss_measure.implementation: repo/src/cbsc_zdc/models/response.py target Jacobian correction; deployed before launch

comparator.why: M0 is the fresh-optimizer control; every screening row pays the same measured 0.021601 optimizer restart, so M0 is the fair yardstick. Its historical raw loss is converted to the common GeV-density measure before comparison.

rows.scientific_motivation: The underproduced ECAL-start prevalence is a named, measured defect, which gives S3 a physics-motivated prior the other rows lack.
rows.queued_behind: S2-response, via _v3/chain_queue.sh, which refuses to start a row until the card is free and refuses to continue past a short row

comparator_rule.statement: The correct comparator for any screening row is M0-fresh at 4.935508412921843 on the common deposited-energy-GeV response-density measure, NOT B0; raw M0 at 4.513572058600877 and raw B0 at 4.483767619419238 are retained provenance, not cross-mode comparators.
comparator_rule.why: Every screening row uses initialize_from, which transfers weights but not optimizer state, so every row starts a fresh Adam. M0 measures what that costs on this bank and horizon. Historical v2-head totals receive the audited +0.421936354321 target-Jacobian offset before any comparison with the bounded spline. Comparing raw losses across response modes is forbidden because they use different base measures.
